name: Close-Grip Incline Barbell Bench Press
description: An incline bench press with a narrow, shoulder-width grip that dramatically increases triceps long head involvement while still loading the clavicular pectoralis major. The incline angle lengthens the triceps long head, which crosses the shoulder joint, creating a potent position for triceps development. This variation is prized for simultaneously developing upper chest and triceps in a single heavy compound movement.

execution.starting_position: Lie on an incline bench (30–45 degrees). Grip the barbell at shoulder-width — this is narrow enough to be a close grip relative to a standard bench press grip. Unrack and hold above the upper chest.
execution.setup_instructions: Set incline to 30–45 degrees. The close grip should be shoulder-width, not inside-shoulder-width. Inside shoulder-width stresses the wrists excessively.
steps: Step 1: Unrack with a close grip, bar above the upper chest.
Step 2: Lower the bar toward the upper chest with elbows tracking relatively close to the body.
Step 3: Touch the upper chest gently and press immediately back to lockout.
Step 4: At lockout, the triceps are under significant tension — squeeze through full extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale before descent, exhale through the press.
common_mistakes: Grip too narrow — inside shoulder-width stresses wrists and reduces stability
Elbows flaring excessively — keep them roughly 45 degrees from the torso
Not pressing to full lockout — the triceps benefit requires complete extension
safety_considerations: Use a spotter for heavier loads
Avoid grip inside shoulder-width due to wrist discomfort risk
The incline creates a longer moment arm on the shoulder — do not use ego weight
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full range from upper chest to complete elbow lockout.
coaching_cues: Tuck the elbows — the close grip is not a reason to flare
Drive through the lockout — the triceps long head works hardest in the extended position
